metadata.note: The Buffalo Bayou, Brazos and Colorado (1853-1870, the first railroad in Texas) and its successor the Galveston, Harrisburg and San Antonio (the 'Peirce Line', renamed 27 Jul 1870) for their independent years, plus the GH&SA branches and the 1905-merged lines run as Southern Pacific. The GH&SA main line from Feb 1883 is NOT in this layer: southern_pacific_sunset_route.geojson draws it (Southern Pacific: Sunset Route / Sunset Limited, 1883-1971) and amtrak.geojson after 1971; the GH&SA main-line features here stop at 1882 as a hand-off, not a service end. Features are split by drawable span x operator: BB&C to 1870, GH&SA 1870-1882 on the main line and 1883-1884 on the branches, Southern Pacific from the 1 Mar 1885 SP Company lease (branches). The 1889 end of the lease, the 1927 T&NO lease, the 1934 merger into T&NO and the 1961 merger into SP are not splits - the trains ran as Southern Pacific throughout, and the map already colours T&NO as SP. Research report: research/branches/galveston_harrisburg_and_san_antonio_railway.txt.

not_yet_sourced: OPEN ends (last CONFIRMED year, not an ending): Southern Pacific Eagle Pass Branch 1885-1951 (Dec 1951 mixed trains 227/228); Gonzales Branch 1885-1951 (Sept 1951 mixed 216/217); Rosenberg - Victoria 1905-1951; Victoria - Beeville 1905-1951. Each needs a last-train date - ICC discontinuance dockets or Texas newspapers on the Portal to Texas History.
ANCHORS (single proven year, not a duration): GH&SA La Grange Branch 1884 (1884 Official Guide letter at Ellinger); Southern Pacific Bay City Junction - Palacios 1906 (Baptist encampment trains).
Victoria 1953 last passenger train: one HMdb transcription (marker 192410, page returned 403); the THC Atlas text reportedly differs. Not drawn - Rosenberg - Victoria stops at 1951 [OPEN].
San Antonio - Stockdale end: TTM-SAGS timeline 1947 vs its own narrative 'probably early 1950s'; 1947 drawn (agrees with OG52 daggers).
Marion - San Antonio opening day: 2 vs 5 Feb 1877 first train, 16 vs 19 Feb formal opening (TSHA-GHSA vs TTM-SP) - year agrees.
Columbus - Schulenburg: TSHA gives 'December' with no year (context 1873); collapsed to 1874.
BB&C Civil War operation 1861-65: passenger continuity not sourced; drawn continuous.
BB&C Richmond - Alleyton: tracks reached Alleyton 'late 1860', no first-train date; 1861 drawn.
Eagle Pass and Gonzales branches: completed 1882 but no dated first train; 1883 drawn.
La Grange Branch passenger end: unknown, before the 1942 abandonment.
Pre-1905 years of the merged roads (NYT&M 1882-1905, GWT&P 1873-1905, SA&GS/SA&G 1894-1905, GL&H/GH&N 1890s-1905) belong to their own reports and are not drawn here.
headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates throughout (see each speed_source and segment note).
branches_deliberately_omitted: San Antonio - Hondo 1882 (GH&SA, western extension before through service): evidence is only station names first recorded in the 1881/1882 Official Guides per BL-TX1, the Guide pages themselves not seen - too weak. The line from San Antonio west is drawn from 1883 by southern_pacific_sunset_route.geojson.
Houston - Clinton (1914 anchor in BL-TX1): ownership by GH&SA (ex-GH&N spur via Galena Junction) is inferred, not sourced.

Port Lavaca - Victoria - Cuero (ex-GWT&P): no positive passenger evidence in the GH&SA era (1905+); freight-only by 1951 (OG52 Table 40 and index 68 dagger at Cuero). Pre-1905 years are the GWT&P's own.
Cuero - Stockdale (built 1907): no source names a passenger train on it; freight-only by 1951 (OG52 Table 68 daggers).
Bay City Junction - Hawkinsville: no passenger evidence of any kind found.

Houston - La Porte - Galveston (ex-GH&N): no post-1905 passenger year found; freight-only by 1951 with bus substitution (OG52 Table 56). SP trains 171/172 Houston - Galveston (1942) are not shown to have used this route.
Strang - Seabrook (Sylvan Beach line, built 1914): no passenger evidence found.
Harrisburg - Stella after 1882: passenger end unknown (freight-only by 1951, OG52 Table 49); drawn only 1853-1882 as part of the BB&C / GH&SA main line.
Wharton - Bay City Junction: no separate GH&SA-era passenger evidence; only Bay City Junction - Palacios drawn (1906 anchor).
Rosenberg - Needville - Damon: ownership as GH&SA not established; no passenger evidence.
research_findings_for_other_layers: southern_pacific_sunset_route.geojson (not edited here) draws three LATER ALIGNMENTS over GH&SA territory for years before they existed: (a) Comstock - Shumla via the Pecos High Bridge, opened 1892 (TSHA-GHSA; BL-TX1 'Former route until 1891' via Flanders, Painted Cave) - 1883-1891/92 trains used the Rio Grande canyon shelf route with two tunnels and a river-level Pecos crossing, 10.7 mi longer; (b) Del Rio - Cabra, relocated 1969 for Amistad Reservoir (BL-TX1 'Former route until 1969' via McKee's, Devil's River, Bullis, Feely) - 1883-1968 drawn on the post-1969 line; (c) the Houston entrance, the 1918 Chaney Jct - West Junction line (TSHA-GHSA) that replaced the 1880 Chaney Jct - Stella entry - 1883-1917 drawn on it. That file's geometry_quality should name these (Rule 2).

southern_pacific_sunset_route.geojson sp-sunset-route-early: operator of record east of El Paso 1883 - Feb 1885 was GH&SA (SP Company lease from 1 Mar 1885). Left as SP from 1883, consistent with the Morgan's L&T layer.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 18.4 mi of an implied 20 mi (TSHA-BBBC: Harrisburg - Stafford's Point 20 mi; BL-TX1 Harrisburg - Stella 7.8 mi, traced 7.9). 100% on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=SP: the UP Harrisburg Subdivision from Harrisburg (east Houston, pinned at the Harrisburg Sub's east end) west through Stella (pinned where the Houston Tap crossed, 7.9 mi out) to West Junction, then the UP Glidden Subdivision to Stafford. This is the ORIGINAL BB&C line, not the later Houston entrance via Chaney Junction (1880/1918), and not the Santa Fe (GC&SF) line that crosses near Stafford. Harrisburg terminal position approximate (within about 0.5 mi). No straight-line leg. Present-day alignment; no relocation of this stretch found in the research, not otherwise checked.

segments.note: First railroad in Texas. Harrisburg - Stafford's Point, 20 mi, opened Aug 1853 (TSHA-BBBC); steam from the outset (locomotive 'General Sherman', late 1852), so no animal-power trim (Rule 5). Galveston connection by Buffalo Bayou steamer; Houston reached only over the separate Houston Tap (not drawn here). End 1870 is the RENAME, not a service end: sold 24 Jan 1870 to T. W. Peirce and associates and renamed Galveston, Harrisburg and San Antonio 27 Jul 1870 (TSHA-GHSA) - the GH&SA feature continues the same track from 1870. Civil War years 1861-65: TSHA-BBBC says the road ran through the war with no new construction, but continuity of PASSENGER service is not stated - drawn continuous, unsourced. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (about one train each way a day), not a timetable reading.
